chunks: 4579 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far عليه السلام about a bondwoman jointly owned by two men, who both designated her as mudabbar. Then one of them permitted his partner access to her private part. He said: "She is halal for him, and whichever of the two dies before his companion, then half of her has become free on account of the one who died, while half of her remains mudabbar."

I said: "What do you think—if the one remaining of them wants to touch her, does he have that right?" He said: "No, unless her freedom is established and he marries her with her consent whenever he wishes."
I said to him: "Has not half of her become free, and has she not come to own half of herself, while the other half belongs to the one remaining of them?" He said: "Yes."
I said: "Then if she makes her master exempt regarding her private part?" He said: "That is not permissible for him."

I said to him: "Why is that not permissible for her, and how did you allow the one who owned half of her, when he permitted her private part to his partner regarding her?" He said: "Because a woman does not gift her private part, nor lend it, nor make it lawful. Rather, she has one day from herself, and the one who designated her as mudabbar has one day. So if he wishes to marry her in mut'ah for something on that day in which she owns herself, then let him contract mut'ah with her for something, whether small or great."

key_terms.تَمْلِكُ فِيهِ نَفْسَهَا: the day in which she has authority over herself
key_terms.جَارِيَةٍ: a female bondwoman or slave girl
key_terms.حَلَالٌ: lawful or permissible in the legal sense
key_terms.دَبَّرَاهَا: they designated her as mudabbar, to be freed after death
key_terms.فَرْجَهَا: her private part; here, sexual access

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on relations with a partially freed mudabbar bondwoman in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out legal rulings concerning a jointly owned bondwoman who was made mudabbar by both owners and later became partially free upon the death of one of them. It clarifies that sexual permissibility in such a case is governed by ownership and legal marriage, and that the woman herself cannot independently render intercourse lawful merely by permission apart from a valid marriage contract.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4579 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abu Jafar Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) about a bondwoman jointly owned by two men, who both designated her as mudabbar (set to be freed after their death). Then, one of them permitted his partner to have relations with her.
Imam (as) said: "She is lawful for him. If either of them dies before the other, then half of her becomes free from the one who died, and the other half remains mudabbar."

I asked: "What if the surviving partner wishes to have relations with her? Is that permissible?"
Imam (as) said: "No, unless her freedom is fully established, and then he marries her with her consent whenever he wishes."

I asked: "Hasn't half of her already become free, making her the owner of half of herself, while the other half belongs to the surviving partner?"
Imam (as) said: "Yes."

I asked: "What if she permits her master to have relations with her?"
Imam (as) said: "That is not permissible for him."

I asked: "Why is it not permissible for her to do that, while you allowed the first owner to permit his partner to have relations with her?"
Imam (as) said: "Because a woman cannot gift, lend, or permit her private parts. However, she has authority over herself for the day that she owns her freedom, and the one who designated her as mudabbar has authority over her for his day.
If he wishes to marry her temporarily (mutah) for something, whether small or large, on the day that she owns her freedom, he may do so."
